newsitem.title: USA: Motorola division cuts prices on some chips.
newsitem.headline: Motorola division cuts prices on some chips.

text.p: Motorola Inc's Customer Specified Integrated Circuits (CSIC) Microcontroller division said Tuesday it cut prices by nearly 50 percent on seven of its one-time programmable (OTP) eight-bit microcontrollers.
The price cuts apply to a recently introduced 68HC708XL36 high-performance microcontroller, Motorola said.
Motorola is the leader in microcontroller sales worldwide with about 18 percent of the 1995 microcontroller marketing according to an In-Stat industry report.
According to Tom Marischen, worldwide marketing manager, "These price reductions reflect our continued commitment to providing quality products and services to our customers, at a low cost."

Microcontrollers included in the price reductions are its 68HC705B16 which carried a previous suggested list price of $8.95 and now carries a $7.95 price; its 68HC705C4A which was reduced from $12.50 to $8.95; and its 68HC705C9A which was reduced from $9.25 to $4.95.
These new suggested list prices are for quantities of at least 1,000, Motorola said in a statement.
